spec.description: Makes the model typed: {"name", "layers": [{"name", "segments": [{"name", "roles": [role]}]}], "temporal_source": "layer.segment.role"}. A role is {"name", "type": category | set | number | text | boolean | time, "values": [what a category or set may hold], "numeric_config": {"min_value", "max_value", "bin_width"} for a number, "text_encoding": bag_of_words | ngrams for text, "key_part": true for the roles that are a record's identity, "similarity_weight" and "security_weight" from 0 to 1}. A role of type ref is a relation to another thing: its value is that thing's key part ("many": true takes a list), "to": "am_…" points into another model, "strict": true refuses a record that names a thing not on record. Layers and segments take the two weights too, and a segment with "together": true scores its roles as one: all have to agree. Every record and question is then checked against it, and records sharing their key parts are versions of one thing.

gql.description: Run one GQL statement against an Ada model. FIND SIMILAR TO (data | glyph) [AT level] [WHERE condition] [LIMIT n] [THRESHOLD x]; LIST ALL [WHERE condition] [LIMIT n]; COUNT ALL [WHERE condition]; COMPARE glyph TO glyph [AT level]; DETECT DRIFT FROM glyph TO glyph [AT level] [THRESHOLD x]; INTROSPECT glyph DECOMPOSE BY LAYER|SEGMENT|ROLE; TREND glyph OVER 30d [AT level] [ALERT ON drift > 0.3]; PREDICT glyph [AT ROLE path] [WINDOW 7d]; AGGREGATE COUNT|AVG|MIN|MAX|SUM [path] [WHERE condition] [GROUP BY path, ...]; FOLLOW glyph [OUT|IN|BOTH] [VIA path, ...] [DEPTH n] [WHERE condition] [LIMIT n] walks the relations a thing's ref roles make; PATH FROM glyph TO glyph [OUT|IN|BOTH] [VIA path, ...] [DEPTH n] finds the shortest chain between two things. A level is CORTEX, LAYER a, SEGMENT a.b or ROLE a.b.c. glyph("d1") is a thing by its key parts, glyph("d1@2") its second version. A condition compares a path with = != < > <= >=, joined by AND, OR, NOT; outcome, store and ts are paths too.

scale.description: What `act` takes for this model; a part left out keeps its default: {"similarity": 0.4, "confidence": 0.7, "records": 3, "exact": true, "must_match": [], "unseen": false}. A record backs an outcome only at `similarity` or closer, it takes `records` of them and `confidence` in the outcome, `exact` lets one identical record stand in for them, a record has to share the situation's value under every `must_match` key to count, and `unseen` true lets the model act on a situation that carries a key or a value none of its wins has recorded.
